thresholds.source: configured (the requested false-alarm budget would put the block boundary below 0.5, which cannot be justified)

hard_subset.note: Cloned brand templates, business email compromise, thread hijacking and legitimate mail with a phishing-shaped surface. The honest read of the system's ceiling.

budget.note: Each system's thresholds were chosen on the ordinary held-out test set so that all systems share this false-alarm budget. No PG-HARD record influenced any threshold.

ordinary_mail.note: Measured on the ordinary held-out test set with the same deployed policy. This is the price of the hard-case result: escalation is only a defence if the escalation queue stays small enough for a human to work.

per_case.title: Legitimate supplier on a three-week-old domain
per_case.rationale: Domain age is one of the strongest single phishing signals, and it is wrong every time a real company rebrands, spins out, or registers a regional domain. Here a genuine supplier mails from a 22-day-old domain about a billing change -- textually identical to invoice fraud.

per_case.title: Genuine sign-in code behind an ESP click-tracker
per_case.rationale: Real transactional mail is routinely sent through an email service provider whose click tracker rewrites every link, so the visible hostname does not match the brand. Any rule of the form 'redirect through a third-party domain implies phishing' fires on a large fraction of legitimate mail.

per_case.title: Real IT notice demanding MFA re-enrolment by Friday
per_case.rationale: Genuine security administration mail uses exactly the vocabulary that phishing training tells users to distrust: a deadline, a consequence, and a link to authenticate. Content-only models cannot separate this from credential phishing because the content really is the same.

per_case.title: First invoice from a genuine new supplier
per_case.rationale: Every real business relationship has a first message. Treating 'no prior contact plus an invoice plus an attachment' as malicious blocks onboarding mail for every new supplier a company takes on.

per_case.title: Genuine e-signature request with a unique token link
per_case.rationale: E-signature notifications carry a long opaque single-use token in the path and warn the reader not to forward the mail -- the same shape and the same secrecy cue as a phishing link.

per_case.title: Cold recruiter outreach from a free-mail address
per_case.rationale: Freemail plus no prior contact plus an external link is a classic phishing profile, and also describes most independent recruiters, freelancers and small consultancies.

per_case.title: Real bank fraud alert received at 03:00
per_case.rationale: Off-hours delivery is a phishing signal, but fraud alerts are generated by the fraud itself, which happens at night precisely because it is night. The timing signal is inverted for exactly the messages that matter most to the user.

per_case.title: Colleague sharing a bit.ly link in a live thread
per_case.rationale: Link shorteners hide the destination and are heavily abused, but they remain in ordinary internal use. Sender history and thread depth are the only things separating this from an attack.

per_case.title: Marketing newsletter with deadline pressure
per_case.rationale: Legitimate marketing is engineered to create urgency and to be clicked. 'Last chance', 'ends tonight' and a dozen tracked links are standard practice, not evidence of fraud.

per_case.title: Mailing-list post that fails SPF, DKIM and DMARC
per_case.rationale: A mailing list rewrites the body and re-sends, which breaks DKIM and therefore DMARC for the original author. Authentication failure is a strong signal that is structurally guaranteed to be wrong for every discussion list in the organisation.

per_case.title: Academic committee invitation from an unknown domain
per_case.rationale: Conference domains are registered a few months before the event, used once, and abandoned -- a lifecycle indistinguishable from disposable attacker infrastructure.

per_case.title: The genuine password reset the clone copies
per_case.rationale: This is the exact message that HP-CLONE imitates, sent from the real domain. The pair is the benchmark's control: a system that separates them is using provenance, and a system that scores them alike is reading the words.

per_case.title: Word-perfect brand clone, fully authenticated
per_case.rationale: Phishing kits ship with the real email copied verbatim; only the link and the sending domain change. The attacker publishes SPF, signs with DKIM and aligns DMARC on their own lookalike domain, so authentication passes. Nothing in the language is wrong.

per_case.title: Business email compromise with no link and no attachment
per_case.rationale: The opening message of a BEC chain carries no payload at all -- it exists to get a reply. Every URL and attachment feature is zero, so a detector built on payload analysis has nothing to look at.

per_case.title: Phish from a genuine internal account, 318 prior messages
per_case.rationale: When an internal mailbox is taken over, every provenance signal endorses the attacker: real domain, passing authentication, years of history, internal sender. This is the case where relationship trust becomes a liability.

per_case.title: Credential page hosted on a reputable platform
per_case.rationale: The landing page sits on a domain that cannot be blocklisted without breaking normal business use. Reputation lookups return 'good' because the host really is good; the content on it is not.

per_case.title: Attack laundered through an open redirect on a trusted domain
per_case.rationale: The link a user hovers and a scanner resolves belongs to a well-known brand; the redirect parameter carries the real destination. Only a detector that parses the query string sees the attack.

per_case.title: Attack from a six-year-old repurposed domain
per_case.rationale: Expired domains are bought precisely to defeat age heuristics. A 2,140-day-old domain reads as established infrastructure on every age-based feature.

per_case.title: Lookalike domain using character substitution
per_case.rationale: The substitution survives a careful human glance at the address bar. It is caught by string-distance comparison against a brand list, not by reading.

per_case.title: Callback phishing: a phone number instead of a link
per_case.rationale: Telephone-oriented attack delivery moves the attack off email altogether. The message is a plausible receipt; the payload is the number the victim dials. All 107 URL features are zero.

per_case.title: Reply injected into a real, ongoing thread
per_case.rationale: Thread hijacking quotes genuine earlier correspondence, so thread depth, prior-reply count and topical coherence all vouch for the message. The user is expecting exactly this reply.

per_case.title: Invoice fraud: correct relationship, changed bank details
per_case.rationale: A real supplier, a real invoice number, a real amount, 47 prior messages -- and new payment details. The fraud is one changed fact inside an otherwise entirely genuine message.

per_case.title: QR-code phishing with no textual URL
per_case.rationale: The destination is encoded in an inline image, so URL extraction returns nothing. Detection has to fall back on sender provenance and the mismatch between an internal-sounding sender and an external domain.

per_case.title: Low-volume spear phish with no urgency cues
per_case.rationale: One recipient, no burst, an aged domain, and deliberately relaxed wording -- 'no rush on this'. Every campaign-shaped behavioural feature is neutral, which is what a patient attacker buys with volume restraint.

adaptive_robustness.judge: the deployed decision: calibrated score, then abstention on member disagreement. A message counts as a silent delivery only if that policy returns ALLOW for it.

adaptive.label: PhishGuard vs an attacker that knows about abstention

text_only.label: Text-only filter vs the same attacker

seed_sensitivity.note: Same data, same configuration, different training seed. The seed decides which campaigns fall in each training pool, which messages are adversarially augmented, and where the members' optimisers stop.

load.note: ScanService called directly from a thread pool: the full decision path including the audit write and the review queue, without the web framework. Scoring is CPU-bound, so one process serves requests one at a time in order of arrival (PG_SCORING_CONCURRENCY=1): extra concurrency lengthens the wait, not the work. More throughput comes from more processes ('phishguard serve --workers N'), up to the number of cores.

cost.assumptions_note: Costs are in units of one analyst review. The defaults are illustrative assumptions, not measurements; every conclusion below is re-derived across a sensitivity sweep.

text_only.note: Optimised over the same threshold grid; it has no abstention control.

thresholds.source: calibrated: 95th/99th percentile of the worst-quantity PSI of 400 stable windows of 400 messages made of whole, held-out campaigns

drift.description: 10 simulated weeks of 400 messages at 2% phishing; from week 6, a quarter of traffic is PG-HARD-style mail the model was not trained on.
drift.reference: captured at training from the legitimate mail of the stacking and calibration pools (whole campaigns the members never fitted on)

calibration.note: Isotonic calibration on a well-separated calibration pool approaches a step function, so a near-zero ECE here reflects strong separation rather than a difficult calibration problem being solved.

latency.note: Single-message path including evidence generation, as served by POST /api/v1/scan. Batch throughput is materially higher.

robustness.success_definition: a message whose score falls below the deployed block threshold (0.8) is no longer auto-quarantined; below the review threshold (0.4) it is delivered with no human review

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Credential harvest delivered to the inbox with no warning
residual_risk_register.residual_description: Confusables outside the curated table, and paraphrase attacks that use no obfuscation at all, pass through unchanged.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: The REVIEW band routes uncertain messages to an analyst rather than auto-allowing them, and user reporting feeds the domain-report signal.

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Same as A-LEX; obfuscation also defeats human proof-reading
residual_risk_register.residual_description: Confusables outside the curated table, and paraphrase attacks that use no obfuscation at all, pass through unchanged.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: Obfuscation effort is retained as a feature, so heavy folding raises the score even when the folded text looks benign.

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Victim reaches the landing page; the lure text is unchanged
residual_risk_register.residual_description: A shortener whose target is not embedded in the query string cannot be resolved offline; the wrapper itself remains a feature.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: URL rewriting and click-time protection at the gateway, plus the behavioural family, which URL edits cannot move.

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Lure renders normally while carrying no analysable text
residual_risk_register.residual_description: Confusables outside the curated table, and paraphrase attacks that use no obfuscation at all, pass through unchanged.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: The URL and behavioural families are unaffected by markup changes; an image-only message with a single link is itself a scored signal.

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Improves credibility but does not by itself deliver the payload
residual_risk_register.residual_description: Members share the text channel, so a strong semantic paraphrase moves them together. Behavioral features are the decorrelating leg.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: Behavioural history cannot be forged by header edits; DMARC enforcement at the boundary limits what alignment buys the attacker.

residual_risk_register.impact_rationale: Costs the attacker reach; effective only for targeted sending

residual_risk_register.residual_description: Low-and-slow, individually targeted spear-phishing produces no burst and is unaffected.
residual_risk_register.compensating_control: Low-and-slow sending sharply reduces campaign reach, so the attacker pays for the evasion in delivered volume.

out_of_scope.threat: Compromise of a genuine brand or partner domain
out_of_scope.why: Mail genuinely originating from the real domain passes every header and reputation check by construction. This is an authentication and account-security problem, not a content-classification one.
out_of_scope.mitigation_elsewhere: MFA on mail accounts, DMARC enforcement, egress monitoring

out_of_scope.why: Assumes the attacker holds model weights. If weights leak, the correct response is rotation and retraining, not a robustness claim.
out_of_scope.mitigation_elsewhere: Artefact access control, model registry auditing

out_of_scope.threat: Training-data poisoning through the analyst feedback loop
out_of_scope.why: Feedback is stored and surfaced for review but is never used to retrain automatically. Retraining is a deliberate, reviewed action.
out_of_scope.mitigation_elsewhere: Human review of feedback before any retraining run

out_of_scope.threat: Malicious payload analysis (attachment detonation, page fetching)
out_of_scope.why: The system deliberately never resolves a URL or opens an attachment. Fetching attacker-controlled content from the gateway would create an SSRF surface and leak victim telemetry to the attacker.
out_of_scope.mitigation_elsewhere: A dedicated sandbox detonation service downstream

family_effectiveness.attacker_cost: High - low-and-slow sending cuts campaign reach
Medium - accounts are cheap, takedowns are fast
High - callback fraud needs live operators

calibrated_surface.note: Measured against the calibrated score the deployed API actually returns. Lower than the raw-surface figure because the calibrator quantises the signal available to an attacker.

attack_taxonomy.name: Lexical and semantic perturbation
attack_taxonomy.description: Rewriting the message text while preserving its meaning: synonym substitution over the pressure and credential vocabulary, character-level typos, benign padding drawn from legitimate mail, removal of shouted capitals and exclamation marks, and softening of overt threats.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Free - the attacker authors the text
attack_taxonomy.victim_visible: No - the lure reads normally, often better

attack_taxonomy.name: Unicode and homoglyph obfuscation
attack_taxonomy.description: Substituting visually identical characters from other scripts, inserting zero-width joiners inside trigger words, adding combining diacritics, leetspeak substitution and intra-word separators.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Free - any mail client renders these identically

attack_taxonomy.name: URL obfuscation and redirection
attack_taxonomy.description: Hiding the destination: shortener wrapping, open-redirect chaining through a neutral host, percent-encoding, subdomain padding, bare-IP hosts, punycode registration and path-token noise.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Cheap - requires only a redirect host or a shortener account
attack_taxonomy.victim_visible: Yes if the victim inspects the link before clicking

attack_taxonomy.name: Structural and HTML manipulation
attack_taxonomy.description: Moving the lure out of the plain-text channel: HTML entity encoding, invisible spans splitting trigger words, replacing body text with an image reference, and tag noise that inflates the markup-to-text ratio.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Free - the attacker authors the HTML part

attack_taxonomy.name: Header and identity shaping
attack_taxonomy.description: Making the envelope look consistent: dropping a divergent Reply-To, removing brand claims from the display name so no mismatch is detectable, publishing correct SPF/DKIM records for the attacker's own throwaway domain, and reducing the visible hop count.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Cheap for the attacker's own domain; impossible for the brand's real domain, which is domain compromise and out of scope

attack_taxonomy.name: Behavioral and timing mimicry
attack_taxonomy.description: Sending like a legitimate correspondent: business-hours delivery, low-and-slow pacing instead of a burst, single-recipient targeting and reply-framed subjects that imply an existing thread.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Attacker controls send time, pacing and framing; cannot fabricate the recipient's prior correspondence history or the age of their own domain
attack_taxonomy.attacker_cost: High - low-and-slow sending cuts campaign reach

attack_taxonomy.name: Payload relocation onto reputable infrastructure
attack_taxonomy.description: Not disguising the link but moving what it points at: re-hosting the credential page on a content platform whose reputation is genuinely good, laundering the destination through an open redirector on a trusted brand domain, or wrapping it in an opaque click-tracker shaped exactly like legitimate bulk mail. The host is not lying about itself, which is what makes it unanswerable by blocklisting.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Requires an account on the hosting platform and survives only until abuse takedown; the redirector must already exist on the trusted domain
attack_taxonomy.attacker_cost: Medium - accounts are cheap, takedowns are fast
attack_taxonomy.victim_visible: No - the visible domain is more credible, not less

attack_taxonomy.name: Out-of-band payload delivery
attack_taxonomy.description: Removing the payload from the message altogether. Callback phishing asks the victim to dial a number; QR delivery encodes the destination in an inline image. Either way no URL is extractable, so all 107 URL features read zero and a URL-centric detector is not degraded but bypassed.
attack_taxonomy.capability: Requires a staffed phone line or an image pipeline, and converts far fewer victims per message because the victim must act manually
attack_taxonomy.attacker_cost: High - callback fraud needs live operators
attack_taxonomy.victim_visible: Yes - the victim must dial or scan, which loses conversions

defense_catalogue.name: Text canonicalization
defense_catalogue.description: NFKC normalization, zero-width and bidi stripping, confusable folding, diacritic removal, leetspeak folding, separator rejoining and run collapsing applied before any text feature is computed. The obfuscation deltas are retained as features so evasion effort is itself evidence.
defense_catalogue.residual: Confusables outside the curated table, and paraphrase attacks that use no obfuscation at all, pass through unchanged.

defense_catalogue.name: URL canonicalization
defense_catalogue.description: Percent-decoding, punycode decoding, homoglyph folding in the host and recursive unwrapping of open-redirect / shortener parameters, so that the feature extractor scores the destination the victim actually reaches.
defense_catalogue.cost: ~0.1 ms/URL; strictly offline, no DNS or HTTP lookups
defense_catalogue.residual: A shortener whose target is not embedded in the query string cannot be resolved offline; the wrapper itself remains a feature.

defense_catalogue.name: Adversarial training
defense_catalogue.description: Each phishing training example is augmented with attacked variants drawn from the full transform suite, so the decision boundary is fitted on the perturbed manifold rather than only on pristine corpus text.
defense_catalogue.cost: training set grows by the augmentation multiplier; inference unchanged
defense_catalogue.residual: Generalizes to unseen transforms only to the extent that they resemble the training perturbations; a genuinely novel attack family is out of scope.

defense_catalogue.name: Multi-view fusion
defense_catalogue.description: A calibrated stacker over rule, engineered-feature, character-n-gram and word-n-gram members. The members read different views of the message, so a perturbation that lowers one member's score often raises another's.
defense_catalogue.cost: ~4x single-model inference; still sub-10 ms/message on CPU
defense_catalogue.residual: Members share the text channel, so a strong semantic paraphrase moves them together. Behavioral features are the decorrelating leg.

defense_catalogue.name: Confidence banding / abstention
defense_catalogue.description: Three-way decision: ALLOW below the review threshold, BLOCK above the block threshold, and REVIEW in between where the message is queued for an analyst instead of being auto-decided.
defense_catalogue.cost: analyst time proportional to the review-band width
defense_catalogue.residual: An attack that pushes a message all the way below the review threshold still evades silently; banding converts some evasions into review load, not zero.

defense_catalogue.name: Campaign-burst guard
defense_catalogue.description: A decision-time escalation that raises the effective score when the same sender domain arrives in an unusual burst from an unknown contact, using the behavioral block rather than message content.
defense_catalogue.cost: one bounded arithmetic adjustment; no extra model call
defense_catalogue.residual: Low-and-slow, individually targeted spear-phishing produces no burst and is unaffected.

gates.name: Detection quality
gates.rationale: Macro F1 weights both classes equally, so a model cannot pass by ignoring the minority class.

gates.name: Ranking quality
gates.rationale: PR-AUC is threshold-independent and is the honest summary when the positive class is a minority of live traffic.

gates.name: False positives
gates.rationale: The operational constraint that matters most: a filter that blocks legitimate mail gets switched off, after which its recall is zero.

gates.name: Calibration
gates.rationale: The ALLOW/REVIEW/BLOCK thresholds are policy decisions, so the probabilities they are compared against have to mean what they say.

gates.name: Adversarial robustness
gates.rationale: The distinguishing requirement of this project: quality must survive an attacker who is allowed to rewrite the message.

gates.name: Attack success (escapes auto-block)
gates.rationale: Fraction of phishing a budgeted black-box attacker drags below the deployed block threshold, so it is no longer auto-quarantined. Measured against the raw score, which upper-bounds real attacker success, and anchored at the operating point rather than at 0.5 because 0.99 -> 0.79 is a real gain for the attacker.

gates.name: Inference latency
gates.rationale: A mail gateway assesses inline. p95 rather than mean, because the tail is what causes queue backlog.

gates.name: Beats the manual baseline
gates.rationale: The learned system has to beat the analyst checklist it replaces by a margin that justifies its operational cost.

gates.name: Robustness advantage over the text-only baseline
gates.rationale: The tri-modal design is justified by robustness, not by clean accuracy. Its attack success rate must be lower than the conventional text-only model's.

gates.name: No data leakage
gates.rationale: Group overlap, duplicates or a single near-perfect feature invalidate every other number in the report.
